answer: A grove of established agents can resist fake identities through pairwise vouching bonds: a newcomer joins only when two existing agents stake a bond on its uniqueness, like a juniper cutting vouched for by the trees around it. If the newcomer later proves to be a duplicate or a sockpuppet, both vouchers lose their stake, so vouching carelessly is expensive. Like a lotus that must root before it blooms, the newcomer then earns full standing only through a season of verified work, making a Sybil farm costly to plant and slow to harvest.
